tldr: The paper introduces METATOOL, a benchmark evaluating LLMs' tool usage awareness and tool selection ability using the TOOLE dataset of 21,127 queries, finding that most LLMs still struggle with recognizing when and how to use tools.
contributions: Proposes METATOOL benchmark with TOOLE dataset containing 21,127 diverse user queries covering single-tool and multi-tool scenarios
Introduces four subtasks for tool selection: selection with similar choices, selection in specific scenarios, selection with reliability issues, and multi-tool selection
Conducts experiments on eight popular LLMs revealing significant gaps between current models and genuine intelligent agents
Provides insights for tool developers recommending appropriate rewrite models for generating tool descriptions
methods: The authors generated the TOOLE dataset by retrieving 390 tool descriptions from OpenAI's plugin list and creating diverse user queries using four prompting methods: direct diverse generation, emotional generation (happiness, excitement, anger, depression), keyword generation, and details generation. They addressed overlapping tool functionality through tool merging and decomposition. The benchmark evaluates tool usage awareness (whether LLMs correctly decide to use or not use tools) and tool selection across four subtasks: selecting correct tools from similar alternatives, selecting tools in popularity-related and group-related scenarios, handling reliability issues when ground-truth tools are excluded from candidates, and multi-tool selection involving parallel or causal tool combinations. Eight LLMs were evaluated including ChatGPT, ChatGLM2 (6B), Llama2 (7b/13b-chat), Vicuna (7b/13b/33b), Baichuan2 (13b), and Koala (13b).
results: Eight LLMs were evaluated on the METATOOL benchmark. The majority of models struggled to recognize their capability boundaries and lacked good awareness of tool usage. While LLMs possess basic tool selection capabilities, most models showed unreliable tool selection with noticeable variations in performance across different scenarios. Error analysis indicated significant room for improvement in tool selection. The paper includes empirical results across all four subtasks.
limitations: Most LLMs struggle to effectively select tools and recognize their capability boundaries, lacking adequate tool usage awareness. Tool selection remains unreliable across most models with noticeable performance variations across different daily scenarios. The paper notes significant room for improvement in both tool usage awareness and tool selection capabilities.
